messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis
Details: 
The failing test `testIssue942()` creates a `DiscreteDistribution<Object>` from a list of two pairs, each consisting of an anonymous Object and a probability. The test asserts that the sample method sampling one element returns an array of length one.

Upon examining the relevant code:

1. The `sample(int sampleSize)` method creates a new array `out` using `Array.newInstance(singletons.get(0).getClass(), sampleSize)`. This means the array component type is taken from the runtime class of the first element in `singletons`.

2. The `sample()` method returns a random element from the `singletons` list according to the probability distribution. It does NOT guarantee the returned object is of the same class as the first element; it only guarantees it is one of the elements in the `singletons` list.

3. The constructor of `DiscreteDistribution` adds keys (elements of type T) to the `singletons` list in the order they appear in the input list. Hence the first element's class used for the array type may not be compatible with other elements returned by `sample()`.

The problem arises because `Array.newInstance(singletons.get(0).getClass(), sampleSize)` creates an array whose component type is the class of the first singleton only. If `sample()` picks an element whose class is different from that type (even a superclass or unrelated subclass), storing it into that array throws an `ArrayStoreException`.

In the test case, the two objects are anonymous subclass instances of `Object`. The first element defines the array type. The sample method might return the second element which does not match the array type exactly, causing an exception.

Thus, the root cause is that the `sample(int)` method assumes all elements in `singletons` are of the same exact runtime class as the first element for array creation, but this is not guaranteed. This results in an exception when a sampled element cannot be stored in the array due to class mismatch.

This diagnosis matches the current bug report describing an exception thrown when using `Array.newInstance(singletons.get(0).getClass(), sampleSize)` if `singletons.get(0)` is a subclass of T but `sample()` returns an object of type T that is incompatible with the array component type.

Recent bug reports are unrelated.

Summary: The bug is caused by the incorrect assumption in `sample(int)` that all objects returned by `sample()` have the same runtime class as the first element, leading to an `ArrayStoreException` when creating the output array.

Next, I can suggest the method locations to fix.
org.apache.commons.math3.distribution.DiscreteDistribution.sample(int)

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
